steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 2-quart casserole dish.
Place potatoes in a large pot and cover with salted water; bring to a boil. Cook until just tender, 15 to 18 minutes. Drain; cool to the touch before peeling. Thinly slice; transfer to a large bowl.

Heat milk in a saucepan over medium heat. Gradually whisk in flour, salt, black pepper, and garlic powder until smooth; cook and stir until boiling and thickened. Add Cheddar cheese and jalapeños; cook and stir until cheese is completely melted. Pour sauce over potatoes; scatter pimentos over top. Transfer to the prepared dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until potatoes are completely tender, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Jalapeño Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: This jalapeño potatoes recipe with sharp Cheddar cheese have a slight kick from the jalapeños. The pimento and jalapeños add a nice color contrast, too.
raw_recipe.name: Jalapeño Potatoes

review.reviewBody: Good, but very, very spicy. Don't get me wrong - I love spicy food. Maybe my peppers were extra hot, since I used home grown jalapeno peppers (canned). I may make these again, but will cut back on the peppers.

I used red potatoes 'cuz that's what I had on hand. I didn't have 4oz jar of jalapenos. I had 2 fresh jalapenos, took out the seeds and chopped up. Tasted just like scalloped potatoes but more cheesy and spice. Thanks for sharing!

This is a great basic recipe and was very quick and easy because of first boiling the potatoes. I did not have fresh peppers so I substituted 1/8 tsp. cayenne powder and 1/8 tsp. red chili pepper flakes. My husband gave it the thumbs up and my three year old seemed pleased. Will certainly make again! Thank you for posting this recipe!

Made for Recipe Group. I left out the pimentos and layered the potatoes in a 13x9. I liked this much better the next day. The taste of the canned peppers gave it a weird taste, but much better after it sat and melded flavors. The guys loved it from the get go! Thanks for the recipe.

I made the recipe as written, except I used two fresh jalapenos diced small, adding them to the milk, flour, etc. so they would soften a bit before putting the potatoes into the oven, and I used new potatoes (skin on). These potatoes were delicious and a nice change. I will make this again!

I made this in November for recipe group, with some changes, but wanted to make it as written before reviewing it since I thought it might matter in this instance. I liked the changes and would make it again with them. As written, my potatoes didn't have a good texture but it may have been a "bad" batch white potatoes. It was also too hot for me with the full can of jalapenos. Not too hot to handle but not pleasant and overpowered the other flavors. However, the first time I steamed (in microwave) red potatoes instead of white and used fresh jalapenos instead of the canned. They were excellent- not as hot (maybe the jalapenos were milder) and didn't have the canned taste. The added bonus of cooking the potatoes this way is using the same dish for all the cooking except the sauce.

These potatoes are definitely comfort food! I used the canned mild diced peppers, as my 8 year-old was eating this. The only major tweak I made was to slice the potatoes before boiling. No need to boil the entire time -- simply remove them after about 10 minutes, as they will continue baking once they're in the oven. I didn't layer either -- just added the drained potatoes into the cheese sauce and dumped them into the baking dish. Next time, I will add more cheese to make a creamier sauce and use fresh, roasted jalapenos since the hubs and I like the heat. Adding bacon is a great idea too!
These were delicious!!I doubled the sharp cheddar & added crumbled bacon but other then that followed the recipe.Bacon makes everything better :D
I used 1/2 cup of fresh jalapenos and omited the piementos. It was so good! My dh said it was the best potatoes he ever had!
Used a fresh garlic and jalapeño. And substitute a small fresh onion for the pimentos.
Made this for our Easter Sunday taters...I added chopped bacon to the milk/cheese mix. It was a big hit and have already been asked twice for the recipe a day later!!!

I made this delicious palapeno potatoes! your family will be begging you for more and guess will be asking for the recipie!!! best best potatoes casserole ever!!!! this became the stample dish for any holiday and gatherings!!! 5 starts
Very creamy and great flavor. This is my new go to for scallop potatoes.

Made it as a side dish for Christmas dinner. Everybody liked it, didn’t tell them about the kick and everyone was pleasantly surprised. I added some extra shredded cheese after it was done baking and let it melt on top and.

Made this for when we had company. I did add more garlic, 1 teaspoon. Most everyone found it lacking. Suggestions for more flavor were bacon and onions. I took the leftovers and added bacon bits and sauteed onions and everyone loved it. I will be making this again but with the added extras.

this is sooo amazing! it is our new favorite additions to suppers. 
dont mind that its a bit salty the salt will be soaked up by the potatoes an it will be amazing. i used red peppers instead an add chilly flakes with the sauce to add lil zip. its so great my kids big to small love it too
I was pleased with the recipe. Everyone liked the spicy taste! I’m wondering if I could make a pan and freeze them? Any advice?
I sliced these potatoes with a mandolin before boiling to make things easier on myself. The flavor was decent, the cook time a little longer than stated.
I used the small potatoes cut in half with the skins left on. Loved the recipe! Will make again.

Very tasty change of pace! Took the advice of other reviewers and cut back on the jalapenos to half of a can and am glad I did. Wow, I like things spicy and with only half the can, it was really spicy. But also very good! I have trouble boiling the potatoes the right amount. The first time I made it, I undercooked them when boiling and this time probably overcooked them. I used 5 potatoes and probably could have used a little more sauce, but that's what I get for adding a potato! I skipped the pimentos. Will definitely make again. Thanks for the great recipe!
